finalAnswer:
Created [Secure banking platform architecture](<temp>\project\.archi-made-easy\architecture-secure-banking-20261110\secure-banking-platform.html).

The design puts identity, not the network, at the perimeter: every request is authorized at the gateway, services talk only over mTLS inside named trust zones, the double-entry ledger is the single source of balance truth, and the payment hub is the only egress path to external rails — with all access decisions flowing one way into a hash-chained audit journal.

Assumptions I made (all listed in the diagram's Assumptions card):
- **No cloud provider named**, so services are provider-neutral — I can retarget it to Azure, AWS or GCP service names.
- **One region**, zone-redundant per component; no multi-region or DR topology shown.
- **No availability, latency, traffic, cost or RPO/RTO figures** are set — nothing invented. The built-in review still flags the ledger and audit journal as lacking recovery objectives; give me your targets and I'll record them.
- **Compliance scope not stated** (PCI DSS, PSD2 SCA, DORA): the controls shown are generic and certify nothing.
- Regulatory reporting, data analytics, and branch/ATM channels are out of scope; the HSM serves the gateway and core banking too, but one representative key path is drawn.

Automated checks passed; not visually reviewed. The architecture review model scored the declared design 98 with no medium or high findings after I added circuit breakers to the synchronous request chain, which it first flagged. In the page, the **Workbench** button and the mode rail (Review, Simulate, Optimize) let you inject failures, scale load and try changes yourself.
